method: Action is the gap between the top of a fret and the underside of the string. A string that runs straight from the nut slot to the saddle sits on a slope, so its height at fret f is the nut height plus the saddle-to-nut height difference multiplied by the fraction of the scale length at which the fret sits. In 12-tone equal temperament that fraction is x = 1 - 2^(-f/12): exactly one half at the 12th fret, three quarters at the 24th and about 0.056 at the first. A saddle height change therefore moves the action at the fret by x times that change and a nut slot change moves it by (1 - x) times, so reaching a target action means moving the saddle by the action change divided by x and the nut by the change divided by (1 - x). At the 12th fret both multipliers are two, which is the familiar rule that the saddle travels twice the wanted action change. Because the multipliers are fractions of the scale, they are independent of scale length: a 24.75 in and a 25.5 in instrument need the same saddle travel for the same action change, and only the fret number matters. The measurement is taken open, from the top of the fret to the underside of the string. Relief is excluded: a truss-rod adjustment bends the middle of the neck and shifts the action at the fret without moving the saddle, so relief must be set first and the neck allowed to settle. Measuring frets run from 1 to 24, the current and target actions accept up to three decimals and must stay between 0.30 and 8.00 mm or 0.012 and 0.315 in, and results are shown in the chosen unit to 0.01 mm or 0.001 in, with the saddle movement repeated in 64ths of an inch. A table gives the height factor and both multipliers for every fret, with the measured fret marked. Adjustments beyond 3 mm of saddle travel or 0.8 mm of nut slot are reported as cautions, and a measuring fret below 5 is described as a nut-height measurement because the nut then sets almost all of the height. Out of scope: saddle position and intonation along the string, string gauge and tension, fret wear and levelling, nut slot angle and back-cut, and instruments where the string leaves a zero fret or a capo rather than the nut. Everything is computed in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Dan Erlewine, The Guitar Player Repair Guide - string action measurement at the 12th fret, saddle height and nut slot adjustment.
Stewart-MacDonald trade manuals and setup guides on string action, saddle shimming and nut slot depth.
Fender and Gibson published setup specifications, which quote action as the string height above a stated fret with the string open.
12-tone equal temperament fret placement: each fret divides the remaining vibrating length by the twelfth root of two, so fret f lies at 1 - 2^(-f/12) of the scale length.
